summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy and GJ tube dependence, and a history of osteonecrosis was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. He was found to have C. difficile infection and septic shock, with worsening respiratory status requiring ICU admission and temporary ventilation. A bronchoscopy revealed multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas and Klebsiella pneumonia, leading to treatment with meropenem and vancomycin. His condition improved over ten days with antibiotic therapy, weaning from support, and stabilization of vital signs. He was discharged to his extended care facility on IV antibiotics with plans for follow-up care.
